facts.raw_span: multiple (approximately 10) bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
The lesions had been growing very slowly in number and size since age 24
had been bleeding occasionally after trauma
right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
recurrent seizures at age 4
lipolymphedema of the lower legs attributed to functional venous insufficiency with insufficient venous pump activity
had been wearing compression stockings for years
similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt, with the father having died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
Sonography: Demonstrated intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations with a maximum diameter of 1.2 cm

Biopsy revealed a well-circumscribed lesion with hyperkeratosis and acanthosis of the epidermis overlying a conglomerate of dilated venous-like malformations with continuous smooth muscle in the upper dermis, partly showing thrombosis
Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant

concepts.why: The patient's family history of similar conditions, including the father's death from an intracranial hemorrhage, combined with the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant and the presence of intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations, supports this diagnosis.
The patient's presentation of multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs, along with the sonography and histopathology results, is consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient's history of lipolymphedema of the lower legs, attributed to functional venous insufficiency, supports this diagnosis.
The patient's history of recurrent seizures at age 4 supports this diagnosis.
The patient's history of wearing compression stockings for years and the presence of lipolymphedema support this diagnosis.

The patient's family history of similar conditions and the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant, although more commonly associated with cerebral cavernous malformation, could also suggest this diagnosis in the context of the patient's vascular malformations.

rationales.F01: Bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules are characteristic of venous malformations and cerebral cavernous malformations.
rationales.F04: Intracranial hemorrhage is a common feature of cerebral cavernous malformations and hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
rationales.F06: Lipolymphedema is a condition that can be associated with chronic venous insufficiency.
rationales.F11: The detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant is diagnostic of cerebral cavernous malformation.
